stories.title: Real2SimLab paper unifies benchmarks for real-to-simulation transfer
stories.summary: A new paper introduces Real2SimLab, a unified platform for evaluating real-to-simulation transfer methods that build simulations from real-world video. It aims to end the fragmented, benchmark-specific integrations researchers now need to compare methods.
stories.more: Real-to-simulation transfer builds simulations from real-world observations, and has long been used in both research and industry. Recently, coding agents have become capable of generating simulation programs directly from video recordings, and several benchmarks have emerged to evaluate them. Because each benchmark defines its own inputs, deliverables, and scoring pipeline, evaluating N methods across M benchmarks requires N times M separate integrations. Real2SimLab is proposed as a single platform to remove that duplication, though the available excerpt does not detail its specific benchmarks or results.

stories.title: New paper proposes Mixture-of-Loops Transformer to improve looped-layer efficiency
stories.summary: Researchers introduce the Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), which reuses keys and values as memory across loop depths instead of just reusing whole layers. The design aims to improve the expressivity-efficiency tradeoff of looped Transformers.
stories.more: Looped Transformers increase expressivity by reusing shared layers across multiple loops, but this reuse costs efficiency. The paper's Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops, rather than simply repeating layers. One variant, MoLT-R, retains the residual stream under a loop-residual design. The excerpt does not specify benchmark results, so how much efficiency or expressivity gain MoLT achieves in practice is not yet clear from the available text.

stories.title: Paper proposes DyLoMo-DiT, a parameter-reusing diffusion transformer with MoE
stories.summary: A new paper presents DyLoMo-DiT, a Diffusion Transformer that reuses a weight-shared loop for its middle layers instead of adding more parameters, while sparse experts still allocate capacity per token. It targets DiT's parameter-storage cost.
stories.more: Diffusion Transformers typically scale by increasing both parameter count and computation, and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) variants expand capacity while keeping per-token compute roughly fixed but still need large parameter storage. Dynamic Looped MoE DiT (DyLoMo-DiT) instead reuses parameters: a weight-shared loop repeatedly applies the middle layers, while sparse experts distribute parameter capacity across tokens. The approach is meant to cut storage needs without the usual MoE parameter growth. The excerpt does not give benchmark numbers, so its actual gains over standard MoE DiTs are not yet established.

stories.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to four SE Asian countries after new export curbs
stories.summary: Nvidia has told partners like Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia, following tighter US export controls on Chinese cloud access. Dealers are reportedly already seeking buyers for thousands of B300 chips.
stories.more: Nvidia instructed server partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. The move follows new US export controls aimed at restricting Chinese cloud access. Dealers are reportedly already seeking alternative buyers for thousands of B300 chips affected by the halt, and one cloud executive described the resulting situation as "chaos." Loans and major data center deals across Southeast Asia are now reportedly at risk. The excerpt does not specify a timeline for when shipments might resume.

stories.title: UK's FCA says Meta refused to let it test Muse ahead of launch
stories.summary: The UK's Financial Conduct Authority says Meta declined its request to jointly test Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, ahead of its UK rollout. The FCA warned of risk from "another force of attack" by agents.
stories.more: The UK Financial Conduct Authority complained that Meta refused to share its Muse personal agent for testing before rolling it out in the UK on Tuesday. The regulator warned specifically against the risk of "another force of attack" from AI agents. The excerpt does not detail what access, if any, Meta did offer, or how Meta has responded to the complaint.

items.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
items.excerpt: The FCA warned against “another force of attack” from agents after the company declined a request to work on joint testing ahead of rolling out its personal agent in the UK on Tuesday.

stories.title: 42 state AGs move to block Character.AI from selling users' chat data
stories.summary: A coalition of 42 US state attorneys general is seeking to stop Character.AI from selling user data during its Chapter 11 bankruptcy. They accuse the company of planning to auction private chat histories from over 21 million US accounts.
stories.more: The attorneys general issued a wave of nearly identical press releases opposing a potential sale of user data as Character.AI proceeds through Chapter 11 bankruptcy. They allege the company is planning to auction off the private chat histories of more than 21 million US accounts. The excerpt does not specify the legal mechanism the AGs are using to try to block the sale, nor Character.AI's response to the allegations.

stories.title: Microsoft details ARTEX, an AI framework state hackers use to automate attacks
stories.summary: Microsoft published the technical architecture of ARTEX, an AI framework in use since July 2026 that runs cyberattacks with specialized agents and little human involvement. State-backed groups from China and North Korea, plus criminal organizations, are already using it.
stories.more: Microsoft's report describes ARTEX as an AI framework that has been in wide use since July 2026, running cyberattacks through specialized agents with almost no human involvement. State-backed groups from China and North Korea, along with criminal organizations, are already deploying it. Microsoft recommends defenses such as honeypots and faked success signals, but acknowledges these may not hold up well against agents that learn and adapt over time. The excerpt does not specify which targets or sectors ARTEX has been used against.
